name: Powhatan
confidence_why: Siebert 1975, the only phonology of Powhatan (extinct since the eighteenth century and known only from seventeenth-century word lists written without prosodic marking), describes an alternating heavy/light syllable count that governs vowel syncope but never mentions stress, so word stress is left undetermined; the popular summary that turns this alternation into a stress rule has no basis in his…
catalog_citation: Siebert, Frank T., Jr. 1975. Resurrecting Virginia Algonquian from the dead: the reconstituted and historical phonology of Powhatan. In James M. Crawford (ed.), Studies in Southeastern Indian Languages, 285-453. Athens: University of Georgia Press.
catalog_locator: pp. 417-418 (section SYNCOPE; weight rule and major syncope on p. 417, minor syncope on p. 418); PDF pages 133-134 of the archive.org scan
catalog_quote: In Powhatan, the low or open short vowels /e/ and /a/ are weak in that they alone are subject to syncope in certain phonological environments, and all other vowels are strong and never syncopated. Within any word, alternating syllables are heavy and light. Syllabic weights are determined by a simple rule. If the first vowel of a word is weak vowel /e/, even-numbered syllables are heavy and odd-numbered syllables are light, but in all other cases odd-numbered syllables are heavy and even-numbered syllables are light. Two independent types of syncope occur in Powhatan, major syncope and minor syncope. A. Major syncope never occurs in basic morphemes or themes of less than three syllables, and does not affect initial or final syllables of words. The weak vowels /e/ and /a/ are regularly subject to syncope in light checked or closed syllables which end in a spirant, that is, light syllables…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote and locator confirmed verbatim in the held archive.org scan of Siebert 1975 (printed pp. 417-418 = PDF pp. 133-134), and the record's negative finding (no 'stress'/'stressed' anywhere; one irrelevant 'accent' on p. 349) reproduces on both scanned layers. The deciding source is a 1975 comparative/philological reconstitution, but it is the only phonology of Powhatan there is or can be: the language went dormant in the 18th century and survives only in Smith and Strachey vocabularies written in ad hoc English spelling with no prosodic marking; Glottolog lists no grammar/sketch/phonology, and direct checks of Wikipedia's bibliography, Glottolog and archive.org turn up nothing beyond Siebert except Rudes 2011 (film-reconstruction essay, low value for stress). Siebert's 'heavy/light' alternation is a parity label governing syncope, never tied to prominence, so not determinable with the Wikipedia
